authors: Hannah E. Urig, Kimberly A. Woodruff, W. Cooper Brookshire, David R. Smith

mcqs.q: In apparently healthy shelter cats with very low FeLV prevalence (~0.8%), the chief limitation of a positive point-of-care lateral flow test is:
mcqs.e: At low true prevalence a positive antigen test is more likely false-positive, giving PPV near 40% in healthy cats.

mcqs.q: How did FeLV test predictive value compare between sick and healthy cats?
o: Predictive value was far better in sick cats
Predictive value was better in healthy cats
NPV was lower in sick cats
mcqs.e: Higher true prevalence in sick cats (~5.3%) drove PPV/NPV near 99%, far better than in healthy cats.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about serial (repeat) testing of apparently healthy cats?
o: It may not meaningfully improve the PPV
mcqs.e: The paper states serial testing may not meaningfully improve positive predictive value in low-prevalence healthy cats.

authors: Kelly Larson, Emma Hart, Rosa Negash, Wendy Novicoff, Nicole Jacque, Samantha Evans

mcqs.q: Did routine clinicopathologic parameters reliably predict cure vs death vs relapse in cats treated with GS-441524?
mcqs.e: Two-sample t-tests showed no statistically significant clinicopathologic differences between outcome groups.

mcqs.q: Among cured cats, what trend was seen in hematocrit and WBC by weeks 2-6?
mcqs.e: Cured cats had HCT and WBC within normal limits by the 2-6 week window, unlike those that died.

mcqs.q: How did owners in this pre-June-2024 US study obtain GS-441524?
mcqs.e: Compounded FIP treatment was unavailable to US veterinarians before June 2024, so owners used unlicensed sources.

authors: Laurie Larson, Jason Hansen, Prakash Ramasami, Jennifer M Miller, Barton J Slagter, Danielle Tremblay, Mayur Patel, Terri Wasmoen

mcqs.q: What effect did prophylactic CPV monoclonal antibody (CPMA) have on the MLV CPV-2 vaccine response?
mcqs.e: 12 of 13 CPMA-treated puppies only seroconverted after a fourth vaccination on day 105 (~15 weeks).

mcqs.q: The CPMA-induced blockade most closely resembles which phenomenon?
mcqs.e: Passive antibody from CPMA blocks vaccinal immunization analogous to maternal antibody interference.

mcqs.q: Given the ~19-day half-life and prolonged blockade, what do the authors recommend for puppies receiving prophylactic CPMA?
mcqs.e: The blockade indicates vaccination schedules should be extended following prophylactic CPMA use.

authors: Marco Genchi, Luigi Venco, Ornella Melideo, Laura Kramer, Marta Fozzer, Alice Vismarra

mcqs.q: What proportion of shelter-intake dogs in this endemic Po River Valley region were positive for circulating microfilariae?
mcqs.e: 173 of 510 dogs (33.9%) were microfilaria-positive, with 15.7% specifically D. immitis.

mcqs.q: What role do unowned/stray dogs play per the study's conclusion?
o: An important reservoir maintaining D. immitis
mcqs.e: Unowned dogs serve as a reservoir keeping D. immitis in the area and raising exposure risk to all dogs.

mcqs.q: Which methods were used to detect infection?
o: Modified Knott's test plus antigen testing
mcqs.e: The study used the modified Knott's test together with antigenic testing.

authors: Ritik Kaul, Jai Bhagwan, Kanisht Batra, Parveen Kumar, Divya Agnihotri
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

mcqs.q: Which three CIRDC pathogens does the new multiplex PCR detect simultaneously?
mcqs.e: The assay targets genes of canine distemper virus, canine adenovirus-2, and Bordetella bronchiseptica.

mcqs.q: Which pathogen was most prevalent among the clinical samples?
mcqs.e: CDV was the most commonly detected agent (25%) among the 55 clinical samples.

mcqs.q: How did the multiplex PCR perform diagnostically?
mcqs.e: The mPCR achieved ~94% sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy.

authors: Violetta Iris Vasinioti, Maria Stella Lucente, Cristiana Catella, Canio Buonavoglia, Nicola Decaro, Annamaria Pratelli, Paolo Capozza

mcqs.q: How does FIP develop in an infected cat?
o: Mutation of feline enteric coronavirus (FECV) to virulent FIPV within an individual cat
mcqs.e: The virulent FIPV biotype arises by mutation of ubiquitous FECV within the host.

mcqs.q: Why does FIP remain difficult to diagnose?
o: Its signs are identical to rabies
No test cleanly distinguishes the FECV and FIPV biotypes
mcqs.e: Non-specific signs and inability to differentiate biotypes force reliance on integrated signalment, signs, and labs.

mcqs.q: What has changed FIP from a once-untreatable disease?
mcqs.e: Antiviral and immunomodulatory drugs now offer effective treatment, though no vaccine exists.

authors: Dawid Janczak, Klaudiusz Szczepaniak, Jagoda Jeleniewska, Olga Szalus-Jordanow

mcqs.q: Tritrichomonas foetus in cats characteristically causes:
mcqs.e: T. foetus is a protozoan causing large-bowel disorders, so it belongs on the chronic large-bowel diarrhea differential.

mcqs.q: Which group showed the highest T. foetus prevalence?
mcqs.e: Prevalence was highest (14.9%) in cats under one year of age.

mcqs.q: What was the diagnostic method of choice in this study?
mcqs.e: The authors used nested PCR (with inhibition-reducing modifications) as the test of choice.

authors: Federica Di Profio, Matteo Carnevale, Fulvio Marsilio, Francesco Pellegrini, Vito Martella, Barbara Di Martino, Vittorio Sarchese

mcqs.q: A hallmark oral clinical sign of feline calicivirus infection is:
mcqs.e: FCV typically causes oral ulceration and gingivostomatitis alongside upper respiratory signs.

mcqs.q: How do persistently infected cats contribute to FCV spread?
o: They become asymptomatic carriers that keep shedding virus
mcqs.e: Persistently infected, often asymptomatic carriers are a key transmission risk in high-density settings.

mcqs.q: Why is vaccination alone insufficient for FCV control?
o: Vaccines themselves cause virulent systemic FCV
mcqs.e: FCV's antigenic diversity and emergence of new variants limit vaccine cross-protection, requiring integrated biosecurity.

mcqs.q: What proportion of dogs in the surveyed LA County communities were vaccinated against leptospirosis?
mcqs.e: Only 22% of dogs were reported vaccinated against leptospirosis despite the recent outbreak.

mcqs.q: What did the survey reveal about owner awareness?
o: Most owners were highly familiar with the disease
Most were unaware of leptospirosis signs or its zoonotic nature
All owners had vaccinated their dogs
mcqs.e: 68% were unaware of the outbreak and 77% were unfamiliar with the signs or zoonotic risk.

mcqs.q: Leptospirosis is best characterized as:
o: A zoonotic bacterial (spirochete) disease causing organ failure
mcqs.e: It is a zoonotic bloodborne bacterial (Leptospira) infection that can cause organ failure and death.

authors: Landsberg G, Mendes J, Kosziwka W, Keys DA, Gordon A, King A, Araujo JA, de Rivera C

mcqs.q: Which drug significantly reduced cortisol and multiple anxiety behaviours in the road-travel model?
mcqs.e: Trazodone 10 mg/kg lowered cortisol, lip-licking, anxiety scores, urination, yawning, and restlessness.

mcqs.q: How did gabapentin 30 mg/kg perform versus placebo?
mcqs.e: Gabapentin showed no significant differences compared with control in this travel model.

mcqs.q: One physiological finding specific to trazodone was:
o: Higher heart rate than gabapentin or control
mcqs.e: Heart rate was higher with trazodone than with gabapentin or control despite reduced behavioural stress.

authors: Kappel I, Materne B, Gansloeszer U

mcqs.q: Compared with cats from private homes, shelter cats in this Strange-Situation study showed:
o: Reduced play, more passive behaviour, and more frequent purring
mcqs.e: Shelter cats displayed blunted play, increased passivity, and more purring, especially after reunion.

mcqs.q: How should increased purring/meowing in shelter cats be interpreted per this study?
mcqs.e: The authors caution that purring and meowing here may reflect stress, not contentment.

mcqs.q: Which factor emerged as influencing exploratory behaviour?
mcqs.e: Outdoor access was identified as a potential influence on exploratory behaviour.

authors: Gazzano V, Curadi MC, Baragli P, Mariti C, Cecchi F, Cavallo S, Sacchettino L, Gazzano A

mcqs.q: What relationship was found between oxytocin and cortisol in relaxed shelter dogs?
mcqs.e: Oxytocin correlated negatively with cortisol, particularly in dogs behaving in a relaxed manner.

mcqs.q: What did oxytocin's negative correlation with body temperature suggest?
o: A possible role buffering stress-induced hyperthermia
mcqs.e: The inverse link with body temperature supports oxytocin modulating stress-induced hyperthermia.

mcqs.q: Which measure did the authors suggest may be the most sensitive index of canine stress?
mcqs.e: Behavioural scoring may be more sensitive than single hormonal or physiological measures alone.
